about: Independent verdict (0017) on #117 and #118 (docs/decisions/0025): assertedBy on every assertion entry, in both the 2026-01-01 map and the 2020-01-01 map (examples/faa-part-107-temporal), which one reviewer read together. The reviewer was a separate agent context. It was given only the corpus passages listed in `read`, fields.md, a JSON before/after of every changed entry, and every entry's id, kind, scope, clarity, evidence and ambiguity question after the change, for judging omissions. It saw the author's reasoning only in the map's own notes and, in round 2, in the author's responses. `sha256` is the final map. `verdicts` is the reviewer's final output, unedited. `rounds` keeps round 1 and how each point was resolved.

p107-diff.json and temporal-diff.json (changed entries, before and after; rewritten for round 2)
summary: Round 1: Every assertedBy value in both maps is supported by the text, including the lead-in cases, and caller is right in all three places it is used. There are no omissions and no draws. One accuracy problem: the 2026 flash-rate-sufficient note says § 107.29(a) and (b) name only the subject of the prohibition, but both paragraphs also name the remote pilot in command. Round 2 (final bytes): In the final version of both maps every assertedBy value and every new note is supported by the text, with verbatim quotations. The round-1 disagreement on the flash-rate-sufficient note is fixed, and there are no omissions.

nits: Every assertion entry in both maps (10 in 2026, 9 in 2020) is in the diff and now carries assertedBy. No entry carries draws. The all-entries files do not include the assertedBy or draws fields, so for entries outside the diff their absence was confirmed only from the diffs. That is sufficient here because no assertion entry falls outside the diff.
reasonable-protection (both maps): '§ 107.39 names only the subject of the prohibition' leaves out 'That human being'. Suggested wording: 'names no one who decides the protection'.

unaided-visual-contact and observer-coordination (both maps): assertedBy lists who holds the ability or duty ('must be able to see', 'must coordinate'). The text never says those persons decide whether it is met. This matches how the § 107.49 lead-in is treated, but it is an inference, and neither note says so.

The same person is spelled 'person manipulating the flight control' in one entry and 'person manipulating the flight controls' in another. Both are verbatim from their evidence, but an engine matching attributions across entries would treat them as two different parties.

unaided-visual-contact: § 107.31(b) lets the ability be exercised by either the pilot plus the controls person or a visual observer alone. assertedBy lists all three together with no indication that they are alternatives.
flash-rate-sufficient (2026): the note's quotation 'no person may operate' is lowercase, so it is verbatim from (a) only. (b) has 'No person may operate'.

One accuracy problem: the 2026 flash-rate-sufficient note says § 107.29(a) and (b) name only the subject of the prohibition, but both paragraphs also name the remote pilot in command.
resolutions: flash-rate-sufficient note (disagree, 2026): taken. The note now accounts for the remote pilot in command § 107.29 names, whose determination is only about intensity.
reasonable-protection note (nit, both maps): taken. The note accounts for the human being protected.
flight control / flight controls, duty-bearer versus decider, § 107.31(b) alternatives (nits): left in the maps as verbatim; recorded as limits in docs/decisions/0025.
